children: Dubai has announced the implementation of a new 80-kilometre (km) Fourth Corridor project, aimed at strengthening the emirate's road network and improving connectivity between Sharjah, Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

Crown Prince of Dubai and Chairman of the Executive Council Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum approved the project, which will extend from Al Shanouf Road in Sharjah to Al Faya Road in Abu Dhabi, according to infograph released by the Government of Dubai Media Office on Wednesday.
The Fourth Corridor will be implemented in two phases.
Phase 1, estimated to cost around 3.5 billion UAE dirhams ($953 million), will extend from Al Shanouf Road in Sharjah to Dubai-Al Ain Road.
Phase 2 will continue from Dubai-Al Ain Road to Al Faya Road in Abu Dhabi.

The corridor will include 72 bridges and 17 tunnels and have capacity for 24,000 vehicles per hour in both directions. It is expected to reduce journey times by up to 60 percent and benefit around 3.1 million people.
The project will also support connectivity with Al Maktoum International Airport and Etihad Rail.
The three existing inter-emirate corridors are Sheikh Zayed Road, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Road and Emirates Road.
(Writing by SA Kader; Editing by Anoop Menon)
